name: # jspec dust and molecular band reference
# All wavelengths are REST-FRAME VACUUM microns.
# lam_min_um / lam_max_um bracket the *band*
species: i.e. the span that should be

name: # shaded with axvspan. lam_peak_um is where the feature peaks (emission) or
# bottoms out (absorption). For band systems with many overlapping heads
# (CO
species: SiO) the bracket covers the whole band system

name: # thing to shade -- the individual heads are in the 'transition' column.
# kind : molecular | pah | silicate | crystalline | ice | carbon | other
#        Used for colouring and for filtering which families are drawn.
# IMPORTANT: band positions for solid-state features shift with grain
# composition
lam_peak_um: shape and temperature -- the amorphous silicate peak

name: # moves between roughly 9.3 and 9.8 um depending on the dust model. Treat
# these brackets as where to look
CO fundamental
notes: Strong in cool SN/AGB ejecta; band head at 4.67 um with a red-degraded P-branch

name: CO first overtone
notes: Band heads at 2.294 2.323 2.353 2.383 2.414 um; the classic NIR CO signature

name: CO second overtone
notes: Weak; needs high column

name: SiO fundamental
notes: Broad; overlaps the amorphous silicate feature so the two must be fitted together

name: SiO first overtone
notes: Band heads near 4.00-4.10 um

name: AlO B-X (0-0)
notes: Electronic band; optical not JWST but kept for cross-instrument work

name: AlO fundamental
notes: Vibrational band; blends with the 11.3 um PAH and SiC features

name: H2O bending
notes: Gas-phase; broad and easily confused with the 6.2 um PAH

name: PAH 3.3
notes: Aromatic C-H stretch; the cleanest PAH band in the NIR

name: PAH 6.2
notes: Ionised PAH tracer

name: PAH 7.7
notes: A complex of 7.6 and 7.8 um sub-features; usually the strongest PAH band

name: PAH 8.6
notes: Sits on the blue wing of the silicate feature

name: PAH 11.3
notes: Neutral PAH tracer; overlaps forsterite 11.3 and SiC 11.3

name: PAH 12.7
notes: Blends with [Ne II] 12.81

name: Silicate 9.7
notes: The classic broad amorphous silicate feature; in emission or absorption depending on optical depth and geometry

name: Silicate 18
notes: Partner of the 9.7 um feature; their ratio constrains grain size and optical depth

name: Forsterite 11.3
notes: Narrow; overlaps PAH 11.3 -- the two are separable only at MRS resolution

name: Forsterite 27.6
notes: Near the MRS ch4-long red cutoff where calibration is poorest

name: Forsterite 33.6
notes: Beyond MRS coverage

name: SiC 11.3
notes: Carbon-star dust; degenerate with PAH 11.3 and forsterite 11.3 at low resolution

name: MgS 30
notes: Very broad; the '30 um feature'. Mostly beyond MRS

name: Amorphous carbon
notes: No band structure; shows up only as continuum slope -- listed so it is not forgotten as a dust candidate

name: H2O ice 3.05
notes: Deep absorption; a broad red wing indicates grain growth

name: H2O ice 6.0
notes: Overlaps the 6.2 um PAH band

name: H2O ice 13
notes: Very broad; easily absorbed into a bad continuum fit

name: CO2 ice 4.27
notes: Narrow and deep; a sensitive ice thermal-history probe

name: CO2 ice 15.2
notes: Double-peaked when crystalline

name: CO ice 4.67
notes: Overlaps the gas-phase CO fundamental band head

name: CH4 ice 7.7
notes: Overlaps the 7.7 um PAH complex

name: CH3OH ice 9.7
notes: In the silicate trough
